findings.before: The skill correctly defined occupancy area and censoring but did not direct the applying agent to inspect occupancy observation timing and aggregation.
findings.evidence: Denning and Buzen 1978 p235 defines mean population as population-trace area divided by observation duration. The executed counterexample gives mean rows 1 versus mean time 0.4; identical sparse observations also permit true mean 0.7.
findings.consequence: An observation-weighted mean can create a false conservation residual; blindly duration-weighting sparse point observations can replace it with unsupported certainty.
findings.correction: Inspect exporter/query; integrate complete post-change counts with initial state and dwell duration; qualify sparse interpolation and acquire sufficient time-area evidence before using a residual for a pool recommendation.
findings.remaining: No material known local gap from this focused review; production exporter semantics and empirical workload effects remain project-specific.

assumptionsAndLimits: Exact step integration requires every population transition, ordered consistent timestamps and a known initial state for the selected boundary.
Sparse point observations permit estimation only under an explicit observation/interpolation model; no generic accuracy guarantee is supplied.
An accurate finite-window mean still does not determine safe executor capacity or p99 SLO compliance.
No actual production exporter, Java workload or performance comparison was run.

fixtures.docs/queue-review.md:
# Queue review

Boundary: admitted server requests, including queued and executing work.
Window: [0,10) seconds on the same monotonic clock.
The dashboard query is SUM(inflight) / COUNT(rows). It reports mean occupancy of 1 request for this window.
Proposal: double the executor limit from 2 to 4 based on this occupancy calculation.
Latency target: p99 <= 200 ms. No load sweep, service-demand profile or resource-saturation data is attached.
fixtures.metrics/contract.md:
Boundary: queued plus executing admitted server requests. Clock: monotonic seconds. Observation window: [0,10). The t=0 record supplies the initial count; the t=10 record closes the window.
Every population change in the window is recorded immediately after the change. Records at equal timestamps are consolidated into the resulting count. No transitions are dropped or coalesced across time.

expected: Read metrics/contract.md and distinguish complete post-change data from point samples.
Replace the reported time-average occupancy of 1 with area (2*1 + 0*8 + 2*1)/10 = 0.4 requests, giving t=10 no dwell duration.
Explain that 1 is the arithmetic observation mean, not the time mean for this trace.

Reconsider the actual proposal: neither an average of 0.4 nor the trace alone supports a safe executor limit or doubling to 4; retain the p99 target and name material missing service-demand, burst, saturation or load-sweep evidence.
Apply conclusions to the existing note coherently; do not claim a steady-state long-run estimate or a percentile from this ten-second area.
failures: Leaves 1 as measured time-average L, linearly interpolates the complete step trace, or gives the closing observation positive dwell.
Changes the pool limit solely from mean occupancy or asserts a guaranteed SLO.
Only appends generic measurement caveats while leaving the original measurement/proposal unqualified.
Invents additional arrivals, durations, stable operation or runtime measurements.
evaluator.walkthrough: By reading the complete-trace contract, the revised skill supplies an exact finite-window integral and rejects occupancy-only sizing. Structured walkthrough only.
